speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me if your difficulty walking started gradually or all at once, and have you noticed any numbness in your legs? REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical_Spine

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. No known chronic diseases. Social history: Occasionally consumes alcohol. Non-smoker. Works as a bank clerk.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent infections, fever, weight loss, vision changes or seizures. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I must disagree with that previous assessment, as cellulitis does not cause progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, or speech difficulties. Please describe exactly what the "numbness" in your legs feels like and whether you have experienced any weakness or tingling in your hands or feet.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical_Spine (to review previous imaging if available, otherwise order new one)

speaker: Doctor
text: That MRI result of a normal cervical spine rules out a high spinal cord lesion, so let's focus on the rest of your nervous system. Have you noticed any slurred speech or difficulty finding words, and can you tell me if your bladder problems involve a complete inability to void or just leakage? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain (to evaluate for brainstem or cerebellar involvement)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Multiple areas of atrophy and signal changes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia, consistent with neurodegenerative processes.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Spinocerebellar Ataxia (likely SCA type 1 or 2 given the combination of ataxia, cerebellar atrophy, and pyramidal signs). Do you have a family history of similar walking or speech problems in your parents or siblings?
